A single small creature, the dhuvvox, drawn as a painterly top-down-three-quarter RimWorld creature sprite in the vanilla RimWorld art style, realistic, on a transparent background. The reference image is the kept adult dhuvvox; reproduce its anatomy, pose, size and silhouette exactly for each facing, and change only the colouring to the variant's.

Body: a small glazed nodule that looks like a lump of slag, a broad, low, flattened dome shell with a fused, glassy, pitted surface, as though cooled from molten ash. The shell is wide and low, much wider than it is tall. A glitter runs across the glazed surface, with small bright glints scattered over the dome and the legs. The surface reads as slag, with a glassy sheen and tiny bubbled pits. The body is one rounded glazed nodule with a short central tube at the front, and has no insect segments.

Legs: thin legs splay outward and low from the rim of the shell, spreading as widely as the adult's, so the creature has a broad, flat, spider-like footprint close to the ground. The leg tips rest on one common ground line.

Colouring: a silver-grey glazed shell with orange glowing accents in the pits, on the leg joints and around the central tube. The glitter is a pale silver-white sparkle.

Facings, shown at one shared scale with the same body height in every view: the south view is the front view, with the eyes and the central tube toward the viewer, and it has the same dome height, leg length and overall height as the east and north views. The east view is a side profile, with the low dome and widely splayed legs shown in profile. The north view is the rear view, seen from behind, with the back of the shell and the haunches toward the viewer and the eyes hidden. The dome top sits at the same level in all three views, and the leg tips reach the same ground level in all three.

Soft painted edges; value and colour contrast against the ground carry the silhouette. Transparent background, no ground, no shadow plate, one creature per facing.
